title: Can music be used within the context of Kino-Eye?

commenti.body:
Im really interested in the films or shorts you consider to be kino-eye. I’ve only watched Man with a Movie Camera but was blown away by the technique at the time. Notably the film had music, but as I recall it wasn’t the original music and might have been a reproduction decades later. Since then I know there’s been multiple versions with different music. 

That being said. If the original artists of this form used music than it’s fair to say it’s another instrument of the art form.

That's a really fascinating question and I believe it hits at the core of the kino-eye theory, its limits and its practical applications. As you have rightly pointed out, montages themselves are inherently manipulated forms of the 'raw' reality that kino-eye claims to capture. Therefore, adding music, which is another highly manipulative medium, does pose a question on the authenticity fo the film.

Interestingly though, Dziga Vertov, the propagator of the kino-eye theory, used music extensively in his most famous work "Man with a Movie Camera". This might suggest that music, when used sparingly and mindfully, can indeed be a part of kino-eye.

At the end of the day, it largely comes down to the intent of the filmmaker and how he/she uses music. If it's used to enhance the rhythm of the images, echo the on-screen emotions, or guide the viewer's attention while keeping the integrity of the captured reality intact, it might be argued that it aligns with the kino-eye principles.

Nonetheless, I recommend seeking multiple opinions and interpretations regarding this, as the subject can be quite subjective and interpretive. Reading more about Vertov, his works, and his commentary on the matter are also likely to offer some valuable insights.

I think (but maybe I am wrong) that the original “Man with a Camera” didn’t have music. 

Unfortunately, I’ve only found this film on YouTube with both versions of with and without music. 

Do you by any chance know where can I find the original film? Or Vertovs writings stating that music can indeed be used within the context of kino-eye?
